primitives.name: Capital Value Manipulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Matters become still worse when the managers of productive property begin to manipulate their industrial and financial policies with a view to producing changes in capital values, of which they inevitably know in advance of outsiders and of which they take advantage with corresponding ease.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When M_t causes systemic instability or regulatory breach.

reasoning_traces.think:
Speculative yield forecasting arises from the interplay between expected returns and capitalization effects, where future yield expectations are translated into present value adjustments. This process is inherently unstable due to the nonlinearity introduced by capitalization factors. The insider advantage emerges as a consequence of asymmetric information, where those managing firms possess superior predictive capabilities over external observers. Asymmetry enables manipulation of capital values through strategic policy decisions, leading to destabilizing feedback loops. These primitives form a closed-loop system where information asymmetry fuels speculative behavior, which in turn distorts capital formation. The failure mode occurs when manipulative actions exceed sustainable bounds, causing systemic shocks. The mathematical structure reflects a dual dynamic: one of forecasting and one of control, both operating under uncertainty. The epistemic closure of these primitives lies in their recursive dependence on each other—forecasting drives capitalization, which enables manipulation, which further distorts forecasting. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle that undermines efficient resource allocation.
